jurisdiction.publisher: Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB / BST), Gatineau, Quebec

domain: railway safety - prediction of casualty outcomes of reported rail occurrences (Canada, federal)
prediction_question: A railway occurrence begins at a known place, time and operating context on the Canadian network (crossing accident, derailment, trespasser event, fire, collision, movement exceeding limits of authority, ...). At that instant, given only pre-occurrence context - where (subdivision, nearest location, province, region, lat/long), which railway, when (date, time of day, season), and what the train was doing (activity type) - will the occurrence result in at least one casualty (fatality or any injury)?
prediction_time: The instant the occurrence begins (OccDate/OccTime, with the documented local time zone via TimeZoneID). Everything the TSB records during or after the occurrence is excluded from the shipped features: TSB's accident/incident type assignment (its taxonomy embeds outcomes, e.g. 'NON-MAIN-TRACK TRAIN DERAILMENT (NO DAMAGE)'), all injury/DG-release/fire/evacuation/damage flags and counts, weather observations taken at the occurrence, track and rolling-stock attributes measured during the occurrence, investigation/deployment/closeout fields, process dates (ENTRY_DT, RELEASE_DT, DAILY_RELEASED_DT, OccClosedDate), the free-text Summary, and even ReportedDate/ReportedTime (the notification instant, which post-dates the onset) - the last is shipped only in the record's provenance, never as a feature. The casualty outcome unfolds after onset and is the label.
target_definition: Binary: occurrence resulted in >=1 casualty. Label source columns: InjuriesIND ('Injuries indicator'), cross-checked against TotalFatalInjuries / TotalSeriousInjuries / TotalMinorInjuries ('Total fatal/serious/minor injuries') and the separate INJURIES table (RODSdb_MDOTW_VW_INJURIES_PUBLIC.csv, 2,710,400 bytes). All are excluded from the shipped feature columns by construction.

split_strategy: MEASURED on the full panel (worker job tsb-004, gate 1.4.0, artifact digest e75a59bb1116e39b980c9fa2f5ea7c2b984fa6ccce4b3286f194de69d2b32309, all 37 gate checks passed, 2026-10-22). Modern-era panel start is measured, not assumed: the taxonomy-era share (AccIncType HISTORICAL/DG LEAKER) runs 25-38% in 1983-1991, 8-17% in 1993-2000, 4-9% in 2001-2013, 2.3% in 2015 and ~0 only from 2016 (0.58%; 0.0% from 2017) - the record's proposed 2004 start sits inside a measured 6.8% early-taxonomy tail, so the panel starts 2016-01-01. Windows by occurrence date: train 2016-01-01..2021-12-31 (7,925 rows, 883 positives, 11.14%), eval 2022-01-01..2024-12-31 (3,831 rows, 463 positives, 12.09%), holdout 2025-01-01..2026-08-31 (1,976 rows, 278 positives, 14.07%); both classes in every split, each positive an independent occurrence (distinct_events == positives). Holdout ends one settling month behind the vintage (data through 2026-08-31 exactly; 109 later occurrences counted and excluded). 139 byte-identical exported rows deduplicated; 7 non-identical OccNo collisions suffixed and pinned via expected_duplicate_ids (id_columns_are_entity_keys=false).

measurements.novelty_prior_art: Web search 2026-10-21: (1) NRC/CNR publication 'Development of a daily updated train derailment impact map...' - a risk-mapping tool built on RODS historical counts, explicitly deferring predictive derailment models to future work; (2) Rana, Sattari, Lefsrud & Hendry (2024), 'Machine Learning Approach to Enhance Highway Railroad Grade Crossing Safety by Analyzing Crash Data and Identifying Hotspot Crash Locations' (doi:10.1177/03611981231212162) - ML analysis of grade-crossing casualty severity from TSB/RODS data, a research paper, not a shipped dataset/benchmark; (3) TSB's own statistics products are descriptive. No public ML-ready rail-occurrence prediction dataset with splits and a scored contract found; mechanical catalog search recorded via check-novelty.py.
